Spec-complete greenfield rewrite of proxima-quic + proxima-http::http3 (RFC 9000/9001/9002/9114/9204/9221/9297 + multipath draft). Sans-IO protocol modules proxima-protocols::quic + proxima-protocols::http3_codec now live inside proxima-protocols (folded from the former proxima-quic-proto/proxima-h3-proto crates); proxima-quic remains its own facade crate, proxima-h3 folded into proxima-http::http3. Tier-1 sans-IO + tier-3 alloc-free leaves + runtime-agnostic facade. Both `native` and `quinn-compat` Cargo features ship indefinitely (no atomic cutover); tokio remains a direct dep of the native facade today because the UDP accept loop uses tokio::net, with a prime Datagram reactor source tracked as the path to tokio-free. Plan slug: i-need-a-full-adaptive-seal.

Sans-IO QUIC + TLS 1.3 protocol crate per RFC 9000/9001/9002/9221 + multipath draft. Tier-1 (no_std + alloc); leaf modules tier-3 (no_std + no_alloc). Publicly consumable outside proxima. A0 scaffolding 2026-05-24.
Sans-IO HTTP/3 + QPACK protocol crate per RFC 9114/9204/9220/9297. Tier-1 (no_std + alloc); leaf modules tier-3 (no_std + no_alloc). Publicly consumable outside proxima. A0 scaffolding 2026-05-24.

Future-shaped Endpoint + Connection facade over proxima-protocols::quic (the `native` feature) AND a quinn-backed shim (the `quinn-compat` feature). Both ship together; consumers pick per build. The native path is quinn-free (gate-enforced by `proxima-http quinn-free (native feature only)` cell) but still depends on tokio because the UDP accept loop uses tokio::net + tokio::spawn — the prime Datagram reactor source is the planned path off tokio. The `TOKIO_FREE_FACADE_ENFORCE` gate cell is staged but not on by default.

Future-shaped H3 server + client facade over proxima-protocols::http3_codec + proxima-quic (the `http3-native` feature) AND h3 + h3-quinn (the `http3-quinn-compat` feature); now lives at proxima-http::http3. Both ship together; the listener picks at runtime per the spec. Native path includes the per-connection driver, the listener with O(1) demux + random SCID, and per-stream backpressure retention. Tokio is required on the native path today (listener UDP loop).

prime async TCP connect + proxima-net::prime (PrimeTcpUpstream: StreamUpstream, folded from the former proxima-net-prime crate) — disciplined-component log; keystone for the consumer relay prime migration. algorithm-development runs first (connect state machine: EINPROGRESS->Interest::Write->SO_ERROR + lost-wakeup correctness). Incumbent: tokio connect; expected parity (connect is per-connection, handshake-RTT-bound) — value is capability not speed.

Prime reactor/read wakeup discipline log. Current finding: readiness epochs moved cached empty `poll_read -> Pending` to ~20.7 ns, and internal trace found/fixed stale kqueue connect-write filters causing repeated empty reactor turns. Post-fix Prime reaches first reactor turn in ~0.31 us, has one turn/read with zero stale/empty turns, and local ready/pending read probes are tied with or faster than Tokio. Remaining blocking echo RTT comparisons are host-scheduler sensitive, not a proven Prime local-path loss.

PostgreSQL wire reintroduction discovery: upstream pgwire 0.28 server-api is tokio-coupled and allocation-heavy; Proxima needs a sans-IO codec crate plus a prime/proxima stream facade instead of embedding pgwire. TLS is existing capability via proxima-tls, not new pgwire-owned protocol work. The target is full PostgreSQL wire capability; phases are sequencing, not scope reduction.

PostgreSQL wire support: proxima-protocols::pgwire_codec (sans-IO no_std no-alloc message codec + session FSM, full protocol matrix incl. messages upstream pgwire omits, folded from the former proxima-pgwire-codec crate) + proxima-pgwire facade: futures-io driver, two mounts (PgWireAnyProtocol for the universal listener's classifier, PgWireListenProtocol standalone), TLS via SSLRequest or a PostgreSQL 17 direct-TLS ClientHello, trust/cleartext/MD5/SCRAM auth, COPY in+out, LISTEN/NOTIFY, portal suspension, cooperative cancel, plus a client half (sans-IO ClientSession, blocking PgClient, PgwireClientUpstream pipe). The SQL engine is a QueryRequest -> PgReply pipe; there is no handler trait. Proof mechanism is scripts/proxima-pgwire-gate.sh + .github/workflows/proxima-pgwire.yml (real-PostgreSQL differential included); there is no discipline log.

proxima::init_telemetry() turns on proxima_telemetry::* macros/#[proxima::instrument] with zero required features; only the tracing::-crate bridge needs the tracing-init feature. init_tracing_default is now a working #[deprecated] alias (fixed 61dff5eb), not dead code.

ResilientSink (telemetry::out::resilient) buffers ahead of any OTLP transport so the shared drain never blocks on a slow/unreachable collector: forever-retrying capped backoff, reconnect-on-error, per-severity retention-horizon shedding (defaults 10/20/30/35/40 min trace-error, validated monotonic ladder), survivable-seconds gauges, aggregated drop announcements. Guarantees liveness, not losslessness.

Hot-path requirements and source rules: 500MB RAM cap, >=55MB/s, <1ms p99, zero-copy and no heap allocation on query/scoring/inner-loop paths, lock-free reads, lock discipline (lock-free > async gate > proxima_lock::Mutex, never a bare mutex, never a spin), no O(n^2), box-free by default, RPITIT for trait-async. Prose rules, hand-curated. AGENTS.md is the single source of truth; this record exists only so ai_docs relations can point at it.

The 21 workspace guiding principles plus the proxima-quic and proxima-h3 overlay axioms. Single source of truth for the principles; ai_docs records the DECISIONS and FAILURES that apply them, never the principles themselves.

The 35 workspace crates in seven layers (primitives, patterns, protocols, stacks, backends-as-features, storage-and-process, apps) with the internal dependency edges read out of cargo metadata, plus the twelve folded crate names that no longer exist. Names mislead in one place: proxima-core is the leaf (error/ring/arena) and proxima-primitives depends on it -- Pipe lives in proxima-primitives, not proxima-core.

ExpertSlab can retain a selected high-precision expert as Arc<Mmap> plus byte range and emits the same per-step ExpertSource without copying the whole expert set. Its memory report keeps heap-owned payload bytes separate from mapped address-space ranges; mapped_bytes is intentionally not an RSS claim.

One DynaExq address is a transformer-layer/expert pair, while the gathered runtime has three independently bound gate/up/down projection sites. ExpertSlab records an O(1) model-layer/projection-to-site table at bind time; a HOBBIT promotion or eviction must change all three sites before the gather snapshot.

Vulkan WGPU embedding exposed a broadcast-reduce output-coverage defect: RMSNorm-shaped folds have logical output [1,1024] but output_axes [0] plus epilogue_broadcast_axes [1]. The WGPU cooperative renderer must use full-rank coordinates, full output extents, and contiguous output strides; after that correction the vector is no longer one-hot but layer-0 parity remains RED.

Default-off qwen35moe-linked-suffix uses partition_between_with_mapping to expand only the final gather through the logits root, then excludes already-returned outputs from standalone suffix evaluation. Every router/residency boundary and current-layer expert binding stays on its existing path. Earlier-layer linking was not selected because dense-attention and SSM placements currently use current-layer ownership. Synthetic tests compare router, gather, and logits bits plus extra original-id cuts; real-model GPU output and performance remain unmeasured for this feature.

SPICE (arXiv:2608.21240) and SpecMD (arXiv:2602.03921) map to an advisory DynaExq prefetch pipe: confidence-aware lookahead may warm low/high ExpertSource entries, but the actual router remains authoritative and misses fall back to exact low-codec sources. Track hit rate, overfetch bytes, page-in wait, TTFT, and TTNT separately.

APEX (arXiv:2608.11688) and MoE-APEX provide confidence-aware pre-attention and layer-level expert prefetch; Beyond Routing (arXiv:2608.08853) keeps selected IDs and router mass fixed while changing post-dispatch aggregation commitment. APEX maps to an advisory DynaExq predictor; Beyond Routing is a separate algebra seam and must not alter residency admission or authoritative routing.

ExpertResidency::prefetch_candidates emits fixed-capacity, confidence-filtered, de-duplicated warming candidates without mutating EMA, residency, or authoritative routing. It is the APEX/SPICE predictor seam; page and evict remain explicit step-boundary actions.

Cloud-Grade Local MoE Inference (arXiv:2606.10493), CoX-MoE (arXiv:2605.17889), Speculating Experts (arXiv:2603.19289), pre-attention expert prediction (arXiv:2511.10676), Multi-Layer Scheduling (arXiv:2602.21626), and NANOZK (arXiv:2603.18046) map respectively to phase-separated prefill/decode scheduling, route-compatible coalescing, advisory predictor positions, three-level scheduling, and an inspectable layer proof boundary. None of their hardware-specific performance numbers transfer to Proxima/Metal.
